estimate.damage_summary: A heavy bowl fell against a household display cabinet, cracking the door glass and damaging the solid-wood door frame and an internal shelf. The photo is consistent with the reported broken pane and substantial impact damage to the frame.
estimate.policy_notes: Sudden accidental impact damage to insured household contents is covered under 2.6, subject to the schedule. Glazing breakage is covered only if optional peril 2.1(e) is agreed; no schedule showing that agreement was supplied, so the glazing and its preparatory/fitting work are treated as not covered under 2.7.3 and 3.5. One attendance may be payable under 7.1.12 because covered timber repair work is also claimed at the visit.

lines.rationale: Drilling is preparatory glazing work under 1.3 and 2.7.2, but the schedule has not been provided to show that optional glazing cover was agreed; without it, this line is excluded under 2.7.3 and 3.5. One drilling operation is plausible for a made-to-measure pane, and the price estimate is stated as if the line were covered.

lines.invoice_text: Installation of the new glass into the frame
lines.rationale: Fitting the replacement pane is glazing work under 1.3 and 2.7.2, but it is not covered unless optional glazing peril 2.1(e) was agreed; absent that schedule evidence, 2.7.3 and 3.5 exclude it. One installation is appropriate for the single cracked cabinet pane, and the price estimate assumes the line is valid.

The pane is the directly broken glazing element, but its replacement is indemnified only if optional glazing peril 2.1(e) is shown as agreed in the schedule; no such evidence was supplied, so 2.7.3 and 3.5 exclude it. A single made-to-measure pane is consistent with the reported breakage, and the price estimate is for a standard equivalent pane if valid.

lines.invoice_text: Repair of dented and gouged solid-wood door frame
lines.rationale: The reported impact and visible gouges support sudden external damage to the cabinet frame under 2.6.1, with repair and restoration of the affected finish covered under 7.1.1(b) and 7.1.7. One flat-rate repair is plausible for the damaged frame section; the estimate allows for local timber repair and refinishing, not upgrading or treating undamaged areas under 7.1.5 and 7.1.10.

lines.invoice_text: Repair and refinish of scratched and chipped wooden shelf
lines.rationale: The description attributes the shelf damage to the same sudden impact, which is covered under 2.6.1; repairing and refinishing the affected area is included under 7.1.1(b) and 7.1.7. One flat-rate local repair is plausible, but 7.1.5 and 7.1.9 limit payment to event-caused damage and do not cover ordinary-use scratches or pre-existing condition.

This appears to be one attendance charge for the contractor’s visit; under 7.1.12 one attendance per undertaking per event is payable in full when indemnified work is carried out at that visit, as the timber repairs are claimed. A single visit is plausible, and the estimate is for a reasonable local vehicle/attendance charge rather than a repeated or additional visit.
